messages:
alex: noticing intermittent packet drops between pods in gpu-pool-uswest2 tonight, seen as retransmits and application stalls. anyone else?
jamie: yup, I saw elevated retransmit counts on a few node pairs around 00:12 UTC. flows to /gpu-training/* were most affected.
suresh: can you paste the tcpdump/ifconfig? also MTU on those nodes?
alex: grabbing quick from node gpu-12 (pod stuck):
```
# ip link show dev vxlan100
3: vxlan100@NONE: <BROADCAST,NOARP,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 0a:1b:2c:3d:4e:5f brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
```
```
# ip -s link show eth0
2: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes 12345678 packets 98765 errors 0 dropped 0 overruns 0 frame 0
    TX: bytes 87654321 packets 87654 errors 0 dropped 12 overruns 0 carrier 0
```
lia: overlay MTU 1450 with underlay jumbo frames 9000 — we do this to avoid fragmentation on encapsulation. dropped tx count on eth0 is small but there are bursts.
suresh: small drops on tx can cause reorders + retransmits at tcp level, especially for large window flows like sharded training. do we have RDMA offload in play?
jamie: RDMA not used for these training replicas, they use gRPC over TCP.
alex: tcpdump around the time shows repeated dup acks then fast retransmit, sample:
```
12:02:11.123456 IP pod-a.51234 > pod-b.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12999, ack 54321, win 64240, options [nop,nop,TS val 123456 ecr 654321]
12:02:11.123789 IP pod-b.443 > pod-a.51234: Flags [.], ack 12399, win 64240, options [nop,nop,TS val 123459 ecr 123456]
12:02:11.124001 IP pod-a.51234 > pod-b.443: Flags [P.], seq 12999:13653, ack 54321
12:02:11.124300 IP pod-a.51234 > pod-b.51234: Flags [.], seq 13653:13653, ack 54321
12:02:11.124500 IP pod-b.443 > pod-a.51234: Flags [F.], seq 54321, ack 13653
```
(not perfect but shows rapid retransmit attempts)
jamie: are there any recent kernel or offload driver updates on the gpu nodes?
alex: kernel is 5.15.90-rc1 across fleet, but we did push mlx5 firmware bump last night to a subset (uswest2b).
suresh: could be firmware + GSO/GRO interaction with vxlan. Try toggling off TSO/GSO on the host for a canary node and run iperf between pods.
lia: also check conntrack max or kube-proxy conntrack timeouts — if conntrack is flushing mid-flight we get weird behavior.
jamie: I'll run a quick iperf3 test p2p across the overlay with 4 streams and large MTU:
```
# on pod-a
iperf3 -c pod-b -P 4 -t 30
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth
[  5]   0.00-30.00  sec  3.45 GBytes   995 Mbits/sec                  sender
[  5]   0.00-30.00  sec  3.45 GBytes   995 Mbits/sec                  receiver
```
but at 10s we saw a 200ms blip and retransmit spike.
alex: stack traces from app show grpc retry loops, latency p95 spiking to 700ms.
suresh: ok here's a quick checklist to narrow: 1) repro with tcpdump+packet counts, 2) check offloads (ethtool -k), 3) test with overlay MTU lowered to 1400, 4) isolate firmware rolled nodes vs not, 5) run iperf with small MSS to see if fragmentation is root.
lia: I'll spin a canary change to set MTU=1400 on vxlan on one node and run training replica for 1h, tagging runs. if that reduces retransmits we have a config mitigation.
jamie: also capture dmesg/driver logs around times (mlx5_core) and check for XDP drops or PF queues filling.
alex: quick ethtool -k output from gpu-12: offloads: tx-checksumming: on; scatter-gather: on; tcp-segmentation-offload: on; gso: on.
suresh: temporarily disabling tso/gso/gro on one host:
```
# on host
ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off
```
then retest.
lia: running that now on gpu-12 canary. I'll report back in ~15m.
jamie: if disabling offloads helps, we can draft a short-lived scheduler rule to avoid affected NICs until vendor fixes firmware/driver.
sre-bot: deploy-started: canary-change/mtu-1400 on gpu-12 by lia at 00:40 UTC
lia: canary results: retransmit count dropped from ~180/min to ~4/min, p95 latency back to ~30ms for the test streams.
alex: wow that's promising. can we correlate which firmware version gpu-12 had vs nodes still flapping?
suresh: gpu-12 is on mlx5 fw 21.28.1010, nodes with problems are 21.28.1008.
jamie: vendor notes mention regression in 21.28.1008 with GSO+vxlan for MTU>1440.
lia: proposal: roll back the firmware on affected nodes to .1008->.1005 or disable GSO/TCO at host level cluster-wide as short term. rollback has risk for throughput.
alex: prefer disable GSO on affected hosts via daemonset that runs ethtool -K on boot and probe, then schedule gradual firmware update once vendor publishes fix.
suresh: agree. also open support ticket with vendor, include tcpdump, ethtool -k, fw versions, and timestamps. I'll take that.
jamie: created ticket #INC-5133 with vendor and attached traces.
lia: rolling daemonset now to mark nodes as mitigated. will monitor for 2 hours and revert if anything else breaks.
alex: thanks team. marking incident as acknowledged. add note to runbook: "vxlan-firmware-gso-interaction" with steps.
sre-bot: incident-note-updated: vxlan-firmware-gso-interaction added to runbook by lia
jamie: quick follow-up: still want to check kube-proxy conntrack settings before we close. low priority but capture.
suresh: noted. I'll schedule a small window to audit conntrack on gpu pools tomorrow.
lia: end of thread for now — will post metrics 2h after mitigation. :white_check_mark:
